Why forms sometimes ask a second question

A captcha is a test a site shows when it suspects automation. People argue about whether the extra step is worth the drop in completed forms. This paragraph only describes that debate.

Support staff should tell a reader what to try next, such as refreshing once or using a different browser, instead of pasting a vendor widget into the help article.

The history of these tests runs from distorted letters to invisible risk scores. A write-up of that history is ordinary prose.
